## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Cūḷapalobhanajātaka* (Ja 263), translated in modern cataloging as *The Shorter Tale of Allure*, is a canonical birth-story preserved in the Jātaka collection of the Khuddaka Nikāya. Set at Jetavana, the story's frame narrative concerns a backsliding monk whom the Buddha summons to the Hall of Truth. Upon confirming that the monk is faltering in his practice, the Buddha remarks that in past times women caused even believing souls to fall into wrongdoing, whereupon he recounts the story of the past. In modern studies, Julius Evola quotes a verse from this Jātaka ("seducers and astute, they destroy the noble life") in his analysis of ascetic detachment and monastic attitudes toward sensual allure [Evola 1995].
